seoTitle: How to Get Data From Other Forms in Jotform Tables
metaDescription: Learn how to pull and consolidate data from separate Jotform forms into one table in 2026 using connected view tabs and relational columns.
intro: Cross-referencing customer profiles or inventory data across different forms usually means manual spreadsheet merging, but Jotform Tables can connect separate forms directly. This guide covers adding a new data view tab linked to another form, filtering which fields display, and setting up relational connection columns for real-time syncing.

steps.heading: Open your primary Jotform Tables workspace
steps.body: Open the primary form project and launch its Jotform Tables view.

steps.heading: Add a new tab
steps.body: Click Add Tab to generate a new consolidated workspace within your table.

steps.heading: Connect to a secondary form
steps.body: Select the Table View layout, choose Connect to Form, and search for and select the target secondary form base.

steps.heading: Select specific fields
steps.body: Mark the specific columns and fields you want populating the new tab view matrix.

steps.heading: Create a relational connection column
steps.body: Within an existing sheet, create a custom data connection column and select the Connect a Table option to link a specific row to another form.

faq.question: Does data stay synced in real time between connected forms?
faq.answer: Yes, the connection is designed so entry updates in the linked form reflect in near real-time within the connected view.

faq.question: Can I connect more than two forms into one table?
faq.answer: Yes, you can add multiple tabs, each connected to a different form, within the same Jotform Tables workspace.

faq.question: Do I need matching field names to connect two forms?
faq.answer: Field mapping is handled when selecting columns, so exact name matches aren't strictly required, but consistent naming makes it easier to track.

faq.question: Can I filter which fields from the other form actually show up?
faq.answer: Yes, you can mark specific columns and fields to populate the tab view rather than pulling in every field from the source form.
